name: navigation-menu
title: Navigation Menu
description: A collection of links for navigating websites.
usageSnippet: <NavigationMenu items=[{ type: "menu", value: "one", label: "Item One", links: [{ title: "Link", href: "#" }] }]/>

parts.name: entry

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: Discriminant; omit (or "link") for a link rendered directly in the bar.

parts.description:
Compound attr-tag API (primary, Marko-idiomatic form). One tag name
carries both kinds — `<@entry .../>` is a bar link (the default kind) and
`<@entry type="menu">` opens a content panel in the shared viewport (its
body renders directly inside the panel) — so entries render in exactly
the order written: links may sit before, between, or after menus. When
any `<@entry>` tags are supplied they replace `items=` entirely for this
render.

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment of the shared viewport relative to the active trigger.

props.name: closeDelay
props.description: The delay before the menu closes

props.name: defaultValue
props.description:
The default value of the navigation menu.
Use when you don't want to control the value of the menu.

props.name: disableClickTrigger
props.description: Whether to disable the click trigger

props.name: disableHoverTrigger
props.description: Whether to disable the hover trigger

props.name: disablePointerLeaveClose
props.description: Whether to disable the pointer leave close

props.name: getRootNode
props.description: A root node to correctly resolve document in custom environments. E.x.: Iframes, Electron.

props.name: ids
props.description: The ids of the elements in the machine.

props.name: openDelay
props.description: The delay before the menu opens

props.name: translations
props.description: Specifies the localized strings that identifies the accessibility elements and their states

props.name: value
props.description: The controlled value of the navigation menu

events.name: onValueChange
events.description: Function called when the value of the menu changes

examples.title: Default
examples.description: Menu items open a shared content panel of links; plain items navigate directly.

examples.title: Rich content panel
examples.source:
import NavigationMenu from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/navigation-menu/navigation-menu.marko";

Everything is copy-paste — no runtime package to install.
examples.description: Use the `content` body to append extra markup — like a featured link or a footer note — to a panel.

examples.title: Disabled item
examples.description: Set `disabled` on a menu item to skip it in the tab order and ignore pointer input.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.description: Zag machines are controlled: a `value` prop without a change handler never moves. Pair it with `valueChange`, or use Marko's bind shorthand `value:=state`.

examples.title: Compound (attr tags)
examples.source:
import NavigationMenu from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/navigation-menu/navigation-menu.marko"; <@entry type="menu" value="getting-started" label="Getting Started">
Introduction Installation Theming
<@entry value="docs" label="Docs" href="#docs"/> <@entry type="menu" value="components" label="Components">
Button Dialog Tooltip
examples.description: Use `<@entry>` attribute tags instead of `items=` to compose each entry directly in markup: `type="menu"` opens a shared content panel (the tag body renders inside it), and the default kind is a plain bar link. One tag name means entries render in exactly the order written — links can sit before, between, or after menus.

examples.title: Precedence
examples.source:
import NavigationMenu from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/navigation-menu/navigation-menu.marko";

<NavigationMenu items=[{ type: "link", value: "ignored", label: "Ignored", href: "#ignored" }]>
  <@entry value="wins" label="Wins" href="#wins"/>
</NavigationMenu>
examples.description: When both `items=` and `<@entry>` attribute tags are supplied, the attribute tags win — the `items=` entry here is replaced entirely.

examples.title: RTL
examples.source:
import NavigationMenu from "@marko-ui/shadcn/ui/navigation-menu/navigation-menu.marko"; <@entry type="menu" value="getting-started" label="البدء">

examples.description: Pass `dir="rtl"` (with `align="end"` to mirror the viewport) for right-to-left layout. Unlike dropdown-menu/menubar's static-wrapper RTL demos, `dir` here is a real @zag-js/navigation-menu machine prop our Input type re-exposes, so this drives the machine's own RTL positioning. The content is static Arabic rather than upstream's live language switcher (English/Arabic/Hebrew), which has no equivalent on this site.

body.description:
Extra markup appended to every open panel — headings, promos, footers.
Receives the item's value; branch on it to render per item. Links belong in
the item's `links` array so the machine can wire them.

composition:
`<NavigationMenu>` renders the whole tree from its input — there is no separate trigger/content/link sub-component to compose:

```text
NavigationMenu (nav, data-slot="navigation-menu")
└── ul (data-slot="navigation-menu-list")
    ├── li (data-slot="navigation-menu-item"), one per entry
    │   ├── button (data-slot="navigation-menu-trigger") — entries with type="menu"
    │   └── a (data-slot="navigation-menu-link") — plain link entries
    ├── div (data-slot="navigation-menu-indicator") — caret that slides under the active trigger
    └── div (data-slot="navigation-menu-viewport-positioner")
        └── div (data-slot="navigation-menu-viewport") — shared animated panel
            └── div (data-slot="navigation-menu-content"), one per menu entry

Feed entries as data with `items=[{ type: "menu" | "link", ... }]`, or compose them directly in markup with `<@entry>` attribute tags — both normalize to the same tree above. A menu entry's panel renders its `links=` array (with an optional `featured` lead link), a `content` body passed to `<@entry type="menu">`, or the top-level `content` render-prop keyed by entry value.
